recordings.title: Ptilonorhynchus violaceus - Satin Bowerbird XC442381.mp3
recordings.creator: James Ray
recordings.location_evidence:
:
satin bowerbird (probably a juvenile, as I've seen/heard him more often than an adult, often hangs around in pine trees nearby), also imitates a red wattlebird (presumably not actually one in the background) at 0:29, plus I think also an imitation of a crimson rosella at 0:38
rainbow lorikeet 0:35
Alisterus scapularis 0:40

Normalized, otherwise would be too faint, however the tradeoff is static.
Recorded on a deck at the back of the house at the provided coordinates, about 5-10 m above ground. This is typical dry sclerophyll forest on a ridge with eucalypts and casuarinas dominating the canopy, in different areas. There are intermittent creeks (more like ponds along the creekline as of Nov 2018) at the valley bottoms east and west about 200 m away.
Feel free to send me additions for background species or suggestions for my recordings, or upload your edited version of the recording, linking to the original and letting me know.
My recording device is a smart phone, a Xiaomi Redmi Note 4X. Recorded straight to mp3.

recordings.title: Dacelo leachii - Blue-winged Kookaburra XC492215.mp3
recordings.creator: Peter Russell
recordings.location_evidence:
:The Blue-winged Kookaburra males usually start this call right on the first glow of light in the eastern sky and also the last glow of light in the evening . They will use the same call during the day around breeding season to attract mates and let other males know their territory .
Their habitat is mainly  semi-arid country along water ways in the Northern Parts across Australia . They are normally stationary birds do not move very far during the year .
Their food consists of Reptiles- small birds- marsupiales - frogs and large insects .
Their nesting habits are usually hollows in Eucalypt trees and sometimes in cliff faces where small hollows may excist '
They are a very nervous bird and will sit very still in foliage so not to be seen .
